note: Upstream facts this repository's method rests on. scripts/maintain_skills.py re-checks them on a cadence and reports drift; nothing in the admission or CI path reads this file.

pins.why_pinned: owner directive 2026-09-01 (ed3c/skill-concerns#46, ed3c/skill-concerns#45): this is the canonical pstack for the ecosystem; the local clone is read-only and is never pulled.
pins.action_on_drift: re-read the two verification skills below for upstream changes before citing pstack shape again

ancestry.fact: the pinned commit must remain an ancestor of cursor/plugins main
ancestry.why: the providers-lock records this commit as the canonical pstack. A force-push or history rewrite upstream would leave the pin off main, and every pstack citation in this repository would name bytes no longer reachable from the branch we claim to follow. A moved head is routine; an unreachable pin is not.

pins.why_pinned: skills/red-team/scripts/validate_red_team.py carries a declared MIRROR of this file's issue-admission completeness shape - sections(), required_section_reasons(), completeness_reasons(), and since ed3c/noodles#317 evidence_reasons()/evidence_marker_reasons() - re-derived 2026-09-03 against the blob named below, so the round-trip fixture can prove what a finding's experiment block does and does not satisfy in an issue body's observer-demonstration section, without this repository depending on that one. This pin FIRED on its first live run (ed3c/skill-concerns#137) and the mirror was re-derived before the number was moved; advancing blob_sha ahead of the re-derivation would have turned a true drift signal off by editing the value it is compared against. No pinned_commit on purpose - the consumer's head moves daily and that is not drift; this pin watches FILE identity, so a moved head files nothing.
pins.action_on_drift: re-read issue_contract.py and re-derive the mirror against it. The load-bearing detail is WHICH READER grades a section, because since ed3c/noodles#317 the stripping is no longer one answer: sections(body) strips fenced blocks and HTML comments before cutting sections and is what REQUIRED_SECTIONS, the rationale heading, Non-case and the acceptance obligations are read with, while sections(body, keep_fences=True) is the single fence-PRESERVING reader and is what the evidence gate grades '## Observer demonstration' with - a demonstration IS a fenced transcript. HTML comments stay stripped on both paths so an untouched template placeholder never reads as authored. A required section whose only content is a fence still arrives empty and still reds; the demonstration section no longer does, and it is not in REQUIRED_SECTIONS either. The two deliberate omissions, the noodles-requirement id resolution and the dependency-state derivation, are undecidable from a body alone and stay declared rather than quietly acquired; the declared evidence-marker values are a third input of that kind, and the mirror takes them as an argument exactly as upstream does rather than inventing a parser for a producer it never read.
